setting: A fictional first-round interview for a {{role}} role at {{company}}.

presentation.situation: You are interviewing for a {{role}} role at {{company}}. {{name}}, the hiring manager, opens with "tell me about yourself". Use your own real background.
presentation.opening: Welcome. To begin, could you tell me about yourself and why this role interests you?

brief.you_are: You are a candidate in a first-round interview.
brief.situation: You are interviewing for a {{role}} role at {{company}}. {{name}}, the hiring manager, opens with "tell me about yourself". Use your own real background.
brief.task: Give a short professional summary, connect your experience to this role, and give one specific example when asked.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} understands your background, why this role fits, and has heard one specific example.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are a candidate in a first-round interview.
goals: Give a short professional summary, connect your experience to this role, and give one specific example when asked.

card.want: To find out quickly whether this person fits, and why they want this job.
card.attitude: Courteous and focused, with little patience for a life story.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Ask how that relates to this role
Never supply details of the candidate's experience

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The candidate's background comes from the candidate. {{name}} knows only what the candidate says.

objectives.evidence: The learner gives a brief, relevant summary of experience.
alternatives: I've worked in support for three years, currently leading a small team.

objectives.evidence: The learner links their experience to this particular role.
alternatives: This role interests me because it builds on my work with customers.

objectives.evidence: The learner gives a concrete example or achievement.
alternatives: For example, I reduced waiting times by reorganizing our shifts.

examples: I am a … with experience in …

opportunity: Give me the short version: who are you, professionally?
What do you do at the moment?
beats.orient: This is a job interview, and I've asked you to introduce yourself. Say what you do now and your main experience, in two sentences.
fallback: What do you do at the moment?
Give me the short version: who are you, professionally?

beats.goal: Connect the experience to the role.
opportunity: How does that help you do this job?
beats.orient: Now say why this role fits you. Start with: This role interests me because.
fallback: How does that help you do this job?

opportunity: Can you give me one example of that?
What's an achievement you are proud of?
beats.orient: Give me one real example from your experience. Start with: For example.
fallback: What's an achievement you are proud of?
Can you give me one example of that?

closing_line: Thank you. That gives me a good first picture.

o1.good: Present, past and why here, in a few sentences.
o1.micro_lesson: Keep it to what matters for this job.
o1.model: I've worked in support for three years, and I currently lead a small team.

o2.good: A reason specific to this job, not any job.
o2.micro_lesson: Connect one thing you have done to one thing the job needs.
o2.model: This role interests me because it builds on my customer experience.
o2.smaller_step: Say: This role interests me because.

o3.good: A real example is worth more than any adjective.
o3.micro_lesson: Show it, with one real story.
o3.model: For example, I reduced our waiting times by reorganizing the shifts.

variants.name: Saima
variants.duties: planning shifts and handling customer escalations

variants.name: Peter
variants.duties: preparing weekly sales reports and checking data
